The SaaS\-cloud\-native version of DataFinder also supports permission control of projects by roles and users, and supports flexible user account and permission control in conjunction with BytePlus Access Control (IAM) in the SaaS\-cloud\-native environment. This article introduces role permissions and user management operations under SaaS\-Cloud Native.

<span id="df17889f"></span>
# Background information

In a SaaS\-cloud native environment, DataFinder can combine BytePlus IAM and its own user role capabilities to flexibly control permissions from coarse\-grained to fine\-grained.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Under normal circumstances, the BytePlus main account that opens DataFinder is the administrator account with the largest authority. Administrators can create multiple IAM sub\-accounts according to the team's business situation, and authorize sub\-accounts with different granularities.


1. When authorizing, the administrator needs to create a sub\-account in IAM first, and conduct coarse\-grained permission control on the sub\-account through the permission policy, and set the project scope of the open DataFinder for the sub\-account.

2. After completing the coarse\-grained permission setting, the administrator can create a user role on the role management page of DataFinder, and associate the role with the created IAM sub\-account by setting the function module of fine grain and the permission range of the data range for the role.


Please refer to the following for detailed operation steps and operation instructions.

<span id="8544a9ba"></span>
# Coarse\-grained permission control: IAM Policy permission control

<span id="a0196917"></span>
## Step1: Turn on IAM permission control

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">DataFinder's IAM Policy permission control function is only supported by SaaS\-cloud native environment and is turned off by default. If you want to use IAM Policy for coarse\-grained permission control, you can use the main account to enable the function.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">After enabling IAM permission control:</div>


   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">After opening, the permissions configured in the Access Control (IAM) of the official website console will be preferentially checked. The permissions configured in the growth analysis product will be double\-checked with the IAM permissions in a "and" relationship.</div>


   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning"><strong>The</strong> <strong>existing sub\-account</strong> users under the same main account need to perform the IAM authorization operation again, otherwise the existing sub\-account will not be able to use the DataFinder normally.</div>


   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If you have previously invited <strong>sub\-accounts across the main account</strong> to become project members, you do not support opening the IAM authorization function. In this scenario, if you want to use the IAM permission control function, you need to contact BytePlus technical support staff to assist in deleting the sub\-account members across the main account. After completion, turn on the function switch.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If the IAM authorization function is turned on and the IAM authorization function is turned off again, the DataFinder permission of the sub\-account will be restored to the historically configured permission status.</div>


1. After logging in to the DataFinder console with your main account, click the Group Settings button in the upper right corner to enter the Group Settings page.

2. Turn on the IAM authentication switch in the upper right corner of the group settings page.


<span id="5d92c36d"></span>
## Step2: Create an IAM sub\-account

The administrator can create an IAM sub\-account according to the personnel situation of the business team. After synchronizing the login link and login account password of the sub\-account to the corresponding personnel, the subsequent business personnel can log in with the IAM sub\-account and use the DataFinder. The instructions for creating a sub\-account are as follows.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/bf8efcfa3eab4cce80c5722613485cc1~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


1. After logging in to the BytePlus console, click **Account Name** \> **Access Control** in the upper right corner to enter the Access Control console.

2. Refer to the [Access Control - User Management ](https://docs.volcengine.com/docs/6257/64977?lang=en)document, create a new user, and then assign the sub\-account to other R & D, data analytics personnel and other roles for subsequent operations.

   * If you need to use a sub\-account to create a project later, when creating a sub\-account, you need to give the sub\-account project global permissions.

   * If you need to use a sub\-account to enter the DataFinder product in the future, you need to add a sub\-account to the DataFinder project and grant the operation permission of the DataFinder.


<span id="38f4b80b"></span>
## Step3: Authorize the IAM sub\-account


1. In the User for Access Control page, click the Add Permissions button after the user to configure the permissions policy in the pop\-up page.

2. According to the interface prompts, select the permission policy authorized for the sub\-account and the open project scope.

   
   |Configuration points |Configuration instructions |
   |---|---|
   |Authorization policy |Select the permission policy to authorize the IAM child account. The current DataFinder provides you with two system preset policies:<br><br><br>* **UBAFullAccess** : has full permissions of DataFinder, and the scope of permissions is equivalent to the project administrator + data analyst role preset by DataFinder. If the project is not restricted in the subsequent limit\-to\-project resource configuration, the **UBAFullAccess** permission scope is equivalent to the preset group administrator role.<br><br>* **UBAReadOnlyAccess** : has the permission to view the DataFinder function page, and cannot operate the function. The permission range is equivalent to the data analyst role preset by the DataFinder.<br><br><br>At the same time, DataFinder also supports you to create a custom permission policy. After the creation is completed, authorize the custom permission policy to the IAM sub\-account. For instructions on creating custom permission policies, see the [New Custom Policy ](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6257/1158323)Help documentation for Access Control. The current DataFinder\-supported custom permission policies are broken down as follows.<br><br><br>* Basic format:<br><br>   ```JSON```<br>```   {```<br>```     "Statement": [```<br>```       {```<br>```         "Effect": "Allow",```<br>```         "Action": [```<br>```           "uba:*"```<br>```         ],```<br>```         "Resource": [```<br>```           "*"```<br>```         ]```<br>```       }```<br>```     ]```<br>```   }```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>* Effect: Support `Allow`(allow access), `Deny`(deny access).<br><br>   * The final scope of permissions actually owned by the IAM sub\-account is the superposition of the role permissions historically configured in the DataFinder and the IAM permissions policy.<br><br>   * The `Deny`in the IAM permission policy takes precedence over the authorization of the `Allow`and DataFinder user roles in the IAM permission policy.<br><br>* Action: Support `*`(all permissions), `Read`(read\-only permissions), `Manage`(administrative permissions) |
   |Limited to project resources |According to the business situation, choose to open the full number of projects to the current sub\-account or only open some designated projects. |
   


<span id="5d8641a0"></span>
### Permission policy configuration example

<span id="aa94453f"></span>
#### Example 1: Open admin/data analyst permissions only for some projects, no permissions for others

You can authorize pre\-set **UBAFullAccess/UBAReadOnlyAccess** policies for IAM sub\-accounts, and only grant permissions for specified items to sub\-accounts.

<span id="3c4bd36f"></span>
#### Example 2: Only some projects have administrator privileges, others have data analyst privileges


|Authorization policy |Permission effect description |
|---|---|
|You can authorize the IAM sub\-account twice. The two policies and project opening scope are as follows:<br><br><br>* Authorize the preset **UBAFullAccess** policy for the IAM sub\-account, open to the specified project<br><br>* Authorize the preset **UBAReadOnlyAccess** policy for the IAM sub\-account to open all projects |<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," /><br><br>The final effective permission range of the sub\-account is the superposition result of the permission policy of the two authorization operations, namely:<br><br><br>* All projects have data analyst privileges ( **UBA ReadOnlyAccess** )<br><br>* Where the specified project is superimposed with administrator privileges ( **UBAFullAccess** ), this part of the project can finally have administrator + analyst privileges. |


<span id="26f1cdcc"></span>
#### Example 3: A historical user has an administrator role for a project, and needs to reclaim its administrator privileges to data analyst privileges

Example scenario description: When a historical existing user grants DataFinder project administrator privileges in the role management of DataFinder, the IAM permission function is currently turned on, hoping to reclaim its project administrator privileges and change it to data analyst privileges


|Authorization policy |Permission effect description |
|---|---|
|After turning on the IAM permission function, you can authorize the IAM sub\-account twice. The two policies and project opening scope are as follows:<br><br><br>* Authorize a Dany\-Manage custom permission policy permission to the IAM sub\-account, open to the specified project<br><br>   ```JSON```<br>```   {```<br>```     "Statement": [```<br>```       {```<br>```         "Effect": "Deny",```<br>```         "Action": [```<br>```           "uba:Manage"```<br>```         ],```<br>```         "Resource": [```<br>```           "*"```<br>```         ]```<br>```       }```<br>```     ]```<br>```   }```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>* Authorize the preset **UBAReadOnlyAccess** policy for the IAM sub\-account, and open the designated project |The final effective permission range of the sub\-account is the superposition result of the permission policy of the two IAM authorization operations and the historical DataFinder\-user role permissions, namely:<br><br><br>* The Deny\-Manage permission result of IAM has the highest priority, which cancels each other with the administrator rights of the user role of the historical DataFinder, that is, the effect of reclaiming the administrator rights is achieved<br><br>* On this basis, the data analyst permission of IAM ( **UBA ReadOnlyAccess** ) is superimposed, and the specified project can eventually have the permission of the analyst. |


<span id="bd55c4fe"></span>
#### Example 4: Some specified projects have analyst privileges, while others have administrator + analyst privileges


|Authorization policy |Permission effect description |
|---|---|
|After turning on the IAM permission function, you can authorize the IAM sub\-account twice. The two policies and project opening scope are as follows:<br><br><br>* Authorize the preset **UBAFullAccess** policy for IAM sub\-accounts, open to all projects<br><br>* Authorize a Dany\-Manage custom permission policy permission to the IAM sub\-account, open to the specified project<br><br>   ```JSON```<br>```   {```<br>```     "Statement": [```<br>```       {```<br>```         "Effect": "Deny",```<br>```         "Action": [```<br>```           "uba:Manage"```<br>```         ],```<br>```         "Resource": [```<br>```           "*"```<br>```         ]```<br>```       }```<br>```     ]```<br>```   }```<br>```   ```<br>    |<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," /><br><br>The final effective permission range of the sub\-account is the superposition result of the permission policies of the two IAM authorization operations, namely:<br><br><br>* The result of the Deny\-Manage permission of IAM has the highest priority, then the specified project is the result of removing the administrator permission in the administrator permission + data analyst permission, that is, the effect that the specified project only has the data analyst permission is realized<br><br>* Projects other than those specified have IAM administrator + data analyst privileges ( **UBAFullAccess**). |


<span id="e11b5425"></span>
# Fine\-grained permission control: DataFinder role management

After logging in to the DataFinder console, you can create a new role in the **Project Center** \> **Rights Management** \> **Role Management** page, and configure the detailed permission list of the role and other information.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">The main account, or the IAM sub\-account with all permissions and management permissions, can refer to the following for role management operations of fine grain.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">DataFinder presets a project administrator role for you. This role has all the operation permissions in the project, and the permissions are large. Please refer to the detailed introduction <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Permission_Management#0cd7e5c4">Preset roles: group administrator, project administrator</a>.</div>



On the DataFinder role management page:


* You can add and manage user roles, and perform detailed role permission control on roles.

* In the future, other users can be invited to become project members by inviting users. When inviting, you can set the project role of the invited user, and then the user who later invites to become a project member has the permissions of the corresponding role, so as to realize the rights control of project members.


<span id="6437678f"></span>
## Step1: Add new roles

On the role management page, click Add a new role, and configure the role name, person in charge, and other information to add a new role.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/b6fd6dcdbc2b4d26abfe7312e8c116cf~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

After the new role is completed, you can view the list of all existing roles in the current project on the role management page, and click a role name to enter the role details page to view and configure the role's permission details.

<span id="710bb024"></span>
## Step2: Configure roles


1. On the **role management** page, click the role name to go to the role details page.

2. Configure feature permissions.

   On the Functional Permissions tab, click Configure to configure the operational permission details for each function module of the DataFinder for the role. Click **Save** when finished.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/ca7c10790c8a42db8c6701535cbc9105~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

3. Configure the **data range**.

   Click **Data Scope** and configure the queryable Actual Attributes, User Attributes, Event List permission details for the role according to the interface prompts.

4. (Optional) Configure **attribute desensitization**.

   If you want to desensitize some of the sensitive properties that the role subsequently queries, you can add a configuration for attribute desensitization for the role.

5. (Optional) Configure **member roles**.

   You can also directly add users who are already in the project as role members, and when added, the project member will have all the permissions configured by this role.


<span id="05cfdb50"></span>
# User management: Invite other users/roles to become project members

<span id="355439eb"></span>
## Prerequisite

Before inviting other users/roles to join the project as project members, you need to obtain the account information of other users/roles. The current invited members have the following requirements:


* **Support inviting sub\-accounts under the same main account** . In this scenario, you need to obtain the sub\-account name and the account ID of the BytePlus main account corresponding to the sub\-account.

   Creating a sub\-account and viewing information about the sub\-account is performed on the User page of the Access Control Console, as detailed in the [Access Control - User Management ](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6257/64977)documentation.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/98d2895ab9224fc3aa74ce2f922f51fb~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

* **Support inviting a role under the same main account as a DataFinder member** , in this scenario, you need to get the role name and the account ID of the corresponding BytePlus main account.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/586f25b5487648fdb01f0c4060fdf30f~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


<span id="88c74764"></span>
## Invite users

After logging in to the DataFinder console, in the **Project Center** \> **Rights Management** \> **User** **Management** page, click + in the upper left corner to configure the sub\-account information to be invited ( **sub\-account name @main account ID** ) or role information ( **role name @main account ID** ) in the pop\-up window, and the role permissions that need to be given to the user.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">When inviting sub\-accounts, DataFinder currently no longer allows cross\-master accounts to invite sub\-accounts as project members, but only supports inviting sub\-accounts under the same master account.</div>


<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/93e68fba6a7848c783a1b7740fb2fc54~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

<span id="a16c0198"></span>
## Follow\-up operation

After completing the invitation operation, you can obtain the invitation link and send the link to the invited members. Corresponding to the invited sub\-account/role, you can log in to the DataFinder console through the invitation link, and use each function module of DataFinder to confirm that there is no problem with the permission details.

<span id="0cd7e5c4"></span>
# Preset roles: group administrator, project administrator

<span id="f72be6a2"></span>
## Group administrator

After successfully purchasing and opening DataFinder in the SaaS\-cloud native environment, the system will create a default group for you, and give the current account a preset group administrator role for the account that purchased DataFinder. The subsequent account has all the operation permissions of DataFinder and can view data such as resource consumption at the group level, as shown in the figure below.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/ef2152518830471f8945c6cfa26d009d~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If an account has administrative privileges for all projects (e.g., IAM authentication is turned on, UBAFullAccess permissions are added to members in access control, and projects are not restricted), then that member has group administrator privileges and can access group management pages such as group overview.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If there is no corresponding permission, the group management page entrance cannot be seen after logging in to the product console.</div>



<span id="106f487d"></span>
## Project Manager

DataFinder assigns you a project administrator role:

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c0a8ee66d5af48c9ac6b78831b6f8b98~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


* After you successfully purchase and open DataFinder in the SaaS\-cloud native environment, the system automatically creates this role for you. After the subsequent project is created, the account created for the project will automatically become the project administrator of the project. You can use this account to control and configure other members and permissions for the project in the future.

* The project administrator role has all the DataFinder functions, data and other permissions under the project, and does not support the modification or deletion of the permission scope of the project administrator role. The permission scope is large, so you need to add members as project administrators carefully. The list of permissions for a project administrator can be viewed by clicking on the project administrator role name in the console.

* When a member account has the permissions of the project administrator and other roles at the same time, the actual permissions of the final member are the combination of permissions of multiple roles.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/b27401c3a71249acbd4e28f970ca6ed1~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


<span id="a2f72fa6"></span>
## Other relevant content

DataFinder also provides you with preset roles for data analytics and data access, which can be applied to most operation scenarios that require data viewing and analysis and data access.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/2118748dcd6043e892865d4105ce6444~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


* You can bind corresponding members for roles, complete access operations, or perform data analytics according to actual needs.

* It also supports disabling these two roles. After disabling, you can recreate the operation role permission rules for data analytics and data access according to actual needs.
